industrial-data-foundation.overviewDesc: Industrial data doesn’t scale through isolated tools. It requires a coordinated foundation to connect, structure, govern, and manage data across systems and sites. Litmus brings these capabilities together in one seamless platform.

capabilities.title: Connect industrial systems at the source

capabilities.title: Run intelligence where decisions happen
capabilities.description: Industrial decisions are most effective when execution happens close to the process. capabilities.title: Protect systems and data across environments

capabilities.title: Govern data as it scales across the enterprise

faqs.question: What is an Industrial Data Foundation?
faqs.answer: An Industrial Data Foundation is the coordinated platform layer that connects industrial assets, structures operational data, runs intelligence at the edge, governs data usage, secures operations, and manages distributed environments at scale.

faqs.question: Why is an Industrial Data Foundation important?
faqs.answer: It helps industrial organizations move from fragmented systems and inconsistent data practices to a more connected, trusted, and scalable environment for analytics, automation, and AI.

faqs.question: What capabilities are included in an Industrial Data Foundation?
faqs.answer: A complete foundation typically includes Data Connectivity, Industrial DataOps, Edge Intelligence, Data Governance, Data Security, and Central Management.

faqs.question: How does this foundation support Industrial AI?
faqs.answer: It improves Industrial AI readiness by making source data more accessible, contextualized, governed, secure, and operationally usable across distributed environments.

faqs.question: How does governance fit into the foundation?
faqs.answer: Governance ensures that data is controlled, searchable, traceable, standardized, and owned so it can be trusted across analytics, applications, and enterprise initiatives.

faqs.question: Why does central management matter in distributed industrial environments?
faqs.answer: Central management reduces site-by-site operational overhead by providing centralized visibility, deployment control, monitoring, and lifecycle management across devices, data, applications, and models.

faqs.question: What is industrial data connectivity?
faqs.answer: Industrial data connectivity is the capability to connect machines, control systems, sensors, historians, and related OT or IT assets so operational data can be collected, normalized, and used across analytics, enterprise systems, and AI workflows.

faqs.question: Why are native connectors important in industrial environments?
faqs.answer: Native connectors reduce custom engineering effort, accelerate onboarding, and improve consistency by providing direct support for common industrial devices, protocols, and systems.

faqs.question: What is the difference between device discovery and tag discovery?
faqs.answer: Device discovery identifies assets and key connection details on the network, while tag discovery focuses on browsing, searching, and organizing the individual signals or data points that need to be collected from connected assets.

faqs.question: Why does protocol flexibility matter for industrial data platforms?
faqs.answer: Industrial environments often combine multiple vendors, communication standards, and network conditions. Protocol flexibility makes it possible to apply the right ingestion approach per asset while balancing performance, responsiveness, and reliability.

faqs.question: What data types should a foundational industrial platform support?
faqs.answer: A strong foundational platform should support time-series data, events, alarms, batches, relational records, and structured data so operations can unify machine telemetry with broader operational and business context.

faqs.question: How does strong data connectivity support Industrial AI?
faqs.answer: Strong data connectivity improves Industrial AI readiness by making more source data available in a consistent structure, reducing fragmentation early, and creating a better base for modelling, analytics, and governed data operations.

faqs.question: What is Industrial DataOps?
faqs.answer: Industrial DataOps is the practice of contextualizing, modelling, orchestrating, sharing, and integrating industrial data so it can be used more reliably across operations, analytics, enterprise systems, and AI workflows.

faqs.question: Why is data contextualization important in industrial environments?
faqs.answer: Data contextualization adds operational meaning to raw signals by attaching asset context, units, timestamps, and metadata, making information easier to understand and use across teams and systems.

faqs.question: What is the role of data modelling in Industrial DataOps?
faqs.answer: Data modelling creates reusable templates and structures for machines, lines, and plants so industrial data can be standardized and deployed consistently across multiple sites and use cases.

faqs.question: How does data orchestration improve industrial operations?
faqs.answer: Data orchestration manages the collection, transformation, enrichment, routing, and monitoring of data pipelines, helping industrial environments maintain reliable flow across OT and IT systems.

faqs.question: Why use a Unified Namespace for data sharing?
faqs.answer: A Unified Namespace creates a shared real-time source of truth where curated data can be published once and consumed by many systems, reducing integration complexity and improving interoperability.

faqs.question: How does Industrial DataOps support Industrial AI?
faqs.answer: Industrial DataOps improves AI readiness by turning fragmented raw data into contextualized, standardized, shareable information that is easier to govern, integrate, and use in analytics and AI workflows.

faqs.question: What is Edge Intelligence?
faqs.answer: Edge Intelligence is the capability to run applications, analytics, AI, machine learning, and language-based workflows close to industrial processes so decisions and actions can happen with lower latency and greater operational resilience.

faqs.question: Why run applications at the edge?
faqs.answer: Running applications at the edge improves responsiveness, reduces dependency on remote infrastructure, and supports resilient local processing for acquiring, storing, analyzing, and displaying industrial data.

faqs.question: How does edge analytics improve industrial operations?
faqs.answer: Edge analytics enables KPIs, anomaly detection, and trigger-based actions to run in real time where data is generated, improving responsiveness while reducing bandwidth requirements and cloud dependency.

faqs.question: What is the role of Edge AI and machine learning?
faqs.answer: Edge AI and machine learning support local inference for predictions, classifications, anomaly detection, and optimization so industrial systems can respond immediately while keeping sensitive data closer to the source.

faqs.question: How do language models support edge intelligence?

faqs.question: What is Agentic Edge?
faqs.answer: Agentic Edge is a guided autonomy approach in which software agents observe conditions, reason over OT and IT data, recommend actions, and execute workflows within defined guardrails to improve troubleshooting and operational consistency.

faqs.question: What is Data Security in an industrial data platform?
faqs.answer: Data Security is the set of controls that protects systems, governs access, secures communications, and supports resilient operations across industrial environments, whether connected, segmented, or isolated.

faqs.question: Why is air-gapped operation important in industrial environments?
faqs.answer: Air-gapped operation supports environments where cloud access is restricted or unavailable, allowing applications, analytics, workflows, and AI to continue running locally without external dependency.

faqs.question: What is the role of a data gateway?
faqs.answer: A data gateway creates a controlled bridge between OT systems and enterprise or cloud environments, allowing approved data movement while buffering, filtering, and reducing direct exposure of production systems.

faqs.question: How does role-based access improve industrial security?
faqs.answer: Role-based access applies least-privilege principles so users only access the data and functions relevant to their role, site, or asset responsibility, improving both security and compliance.

faqs.question: Why are audit trails important for industrial operations?
faqs.answer: Audit trails provide visibility into user activity, system changes, and operational events, helping teams investigate incidents, maintain accountability, and support compliance requirements.

faqs.question: How do encryption and certificate management support secure operations?
faqs.answer: Encryption protects data in transit, while certificate management helps establish trusted communication between devices, services, and systems, improving integrity and reducing risk across distributed environments.

faqs.question: What is Data Governance in an industrial data platform?
faqs.answer: Data Governance is the framework that defines how industrial data is controlled, described, traced, standardized, and owned so it can be used consistently and trusted across systems and teams.

faqs.question: Why is policy and control important for industrial data?
faqs.answer: Policy and control help enforce rules for how data moves, where it is routed, how long it is retained, and what approvals or protections apply, reducing risk as data operations scale.

faqs.question: What is the role of a metadata catalog in data governance?
faqs.answer: A metadata catalog makes assets, tags, models, and data products easier to find and trust by organizing them in a searchable layer with consistent descriptions and context.

faqs.question: Why does data lineage matter in industrial environments?
faqs.answer: Data lineage shows where data originated, how it changed, and where it is consumed, helping improve trust, speed troubleshooting, and support better governance decisions across complex data pipelines.

faqs.question: How does a business glossary improve governance?
faqs.answer: A business glossary standardizes business and technical definitions so teams interpret metrics, processes, and data elements consistently across systems and functions.

faqs.question: Why are ownership and documentation important for data trust?
faqs.answer: Ownership and documentation create accountability for data assets and preserve the context needed to use them correctly, improving stewardship, onboarding, and long-term operational continuity.

faqs.question: What is Central Management in an industrial data platform?
faqs.answer: Central Management is the operational control layer that provides centralized visibility and lifecycle management for edge fleets, data, applications, operational models, and AI models across distributed industrial environments.

faqs.question: Why is centralized device management important for industrial scale?
faqs.answer: Centralized device management reduces site-by-site operational overhead by enabling remote provisioning, configuration, monitoring, and updates across edge fleets while improving consistency and visibility.

faqs.question: How does Central Management improve data reliability?

faqs.question: Why is application lifecycle management important in distributed environments?
faqs.answer: Application lifecycle management helps control deployment, versioning, rollout, and rollback across sites, reducing operational risk and improving the repeatability of software delivery.

faqs.question: What is the role of data model management in Central Management?

faqs.question: How does AI model management support industrial AI programs?
